Beginning in 1974, the fictitious '''Peter Orno''' (alternatively, '''Peter Ørno''', '''P.&nbsp;Ørno''', and '''P.&nbsp;Orno''') appeared as the author of research papers in mathematics. According to [[Robert Phelps]],<ref name=Phelpsharvtxt>{{harvtxt|Phelps|2002}}</ref> the name "P.&nbsp;Orno" is a [[pseudonym]] that was inspired by "porno", an abbreviation for "[[pornography]]".<ref name="Phelps"/><ref name="Diestel">In the index to his ''Sequences and series in Banach spaces'', [[Joseph Diestel]] places Peter Orno under the letter&nbsp;"p" as&nbsp;"P.&nbsp;ORNO", with all-capital letters in Diestel's original. {{harv|Diestel|1984|p=259}}.</ref> Orno's short papers have been called "elegant" contributions to [[functional analysis]]. Orno's theorem on [[linear operator]]s is important in the theory of [[Banach space]]s. Research mathematicians have written acknowledgments that have thanked Orno for stimulating discussions and for Orno's generosity in allowing others to publish his results. The [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s journals have also published more than a dozen [[mathematical problem|problem]]s whose solutions were submitted in the name of Orno.

==Biography==
[[File:OSU Numbers Garden.JPG|thumb| alt=Several tall Arabic numerals standing upright in a lawn |Peter Orno's publications list his affiliation as [[Ohio State University]], site of the ''Garden of Constants''.<ref>The ''Garden of Constants'' is located at Ohio State University, according to {{harv|Ross Mathematics Program|2012|loc=Caption "Garden of Constants at Ohio State"}}:<p>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.osu.edu/ross/|access-date=12 April 2012|title=Ross Mathematics Program June 18 –July 27, 2012|publisher=Ohio State University|last=Ross Mathematics Program|author-link=Ross Mathematics Program|year=2012}}</p></ref>]]
Peter Orno appears as the author of short papers written by an anonymous mathematician; thus "Peter Orno" is a [[pseudonym]]. According to [[Robert R. Phelps]],<ref name=Phelpsharvtxt/> the name "P.&nbsp;Orno" was inspired by "porno", a shortening of "pornography".<ref name="Phelps"/><ref name="Diestel"/>

Orno's papers list his affiliation as the Department of Mathematics at [[Ohio State University]]. This affiliation is confirmed in the description of Orno as a "special creation" at Ohio&nbsp;State in Pietsch's ''History of Banach spaces and linear operators''.<ref>{{harvtxt|Pietsch|2007|p=602}}</ref>
The publications list of Ohio State mathematician [[Gerald Edgar]] includes two items that were published under the name of Orno. Edgar indicates that he published them "as Peter Ørno".<ref>Gerald A. Edgar, [http://www.math.osu.edu/~edgar.2/publications/pubs.html Publications], Ohio State University. Retrieved March 18, 2012; archived by WebCite at. Items that Edgar claims as his work, but identifies as having been attributed to "Peter Ørno", are the problem proposed in ''Mathematics Magazine'' 52 (1979), 179, and the problem solution presented in ''American Mathematical Monthly'' 113 (2006) 572–573.</ref>

==Research==
His papers feature "surprisingly simple" proofs and solutions to open problems in [[functional analysis]] and [[approximation theory]], according <!-- Wulbert on 1977 Kent St paper --> to reviewers from ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'': In one case, Orno's "elegant" approach was contrasted with the previously known "elementary, but masochistic" approach.<!-- Bennet reviewing PAMS --> Peter Orno's "permanent interest and sharp criticism stimulated" the "work" on ''Lectures on Banach spaces of analytic functions'' by Aleksander Pełczyński, which includes several of Orno's unpublished results.<ref>{{harvtxt|Pełczyński|1977|p=2}}</ref> Tomczak-Jaegermann thanked Peter Orno for his stimulating discussions.<ref>{{harvtxt|Tomczak-Jaegermann|1979|p=273}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
Peter Orno has published in research journals and in collections; his papers have always been short, having lengths between one and three pages. Orno has also established himself as a formidable solver of mathematical problems in peer-reviewed journals published by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].

===Research papers===
* {{cite journal
 |last=Ørno |first=P.
 |year=1974
 |title=On Banach lattices of operators
 |journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
 |volume=19 |pages=264–265
 |doi=10.1007/BF02757723 | doi-access=
 |mr=374859
 |issue=3
 |s2cid=122083903
 }}<br/><br/>According to ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' ({{MR|374859}}), this paper proves the following theorem, which has come to be known as "''Orno's theorem''": Suppose that ''E'' and ''F'' are [[vector lattice|Banach lattice]]s, where ''F'' is an [[infinite-dimensional vector space]] that  contains no [[Riesz space|Riesz subspace]] that is uniformly [[continuous linear operator|isomorphic]] to the [[sequence space]] equipped with the [[supremum norm]]. If each linear operator in the uniform closure of the [[finite-rank operator]]s from E to F has a Riesz decomposition as the difference of two [[positive operator]]s, then E can be renormed so that it is an [[Banach lattice|L-space]] (in the sense of Kakutani and Birkhoff).<ref>

* {{cite journal
 |last=Ørno |first=P.
 |year=1976
 |title=A note on unconditionally converging series in ''L''<sub>''p''</sub> 
 |journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]] 
 |volume=59 |issue=2 |pages=252–254
 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1976-0458156-7
 |jstor=2041478
 |mr=458156
 |doi-access=free}}<br/><br/>According to ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' ({{MR|458156}}), Orno proved the following theorem: The series Σ''f''<sub>''k''</sub>  [[unconditional convergence|unconditionally converges]] in the [[Lp space|Lebesgue space]] of [[absolutely integrable function]]s ''L''<sub>1</sub>[0,1] if and only if, for each ''k'' and every ''t'', we have ''f''<sub>''k''</sub>(''t'')=''a''<sub>''k''</sub>''g''(''t'')''w''<sub>''k''</sub>(''t''), for some sequence (''a''<sub>''k''</sub>)∈''l''<sub>2</sub>, some function ''g''∈''L''<sub>2</sub>[0,1], and for some [[orthonormal sequence]] (''w''<sub>''k''</sub>) in ''L''<sub>2</sub>[0,2] {{MR|458156}}. Another result is what [[Joseph Diestel]] described as the "elegant proof" by Orno of a theorem of Bennet, Maurey and Nahoum.<ref>{{harvtxt|Diestel|1984|p=[https://books.google.com/books?id=UVmqAAAAIAAJ&q=orno 190]}}</ref><br/><br/>

 |last=Ørno |first=P.
 |year=1977
 |chapter=A separable reflexive Banach space having no finite dimensional Čebyšev subspaces
 |editor1-last=Baker |editor1-first=J.
 |editor2-last=Cleaver |editor2-first=C.
 |editor3-last=Diestel  |editor3-first=J. 
 |doi=10.1007/BFb0069208 
 |title=Banach Spaces of Analytic Functions: Proceedings of the Pelczynski Conference Held at Kent State University, Kent, Ohio, July 12–17, 1976
 |volume=604 |pages=73–75 
 |series=[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]] 
 |publisher=[[Springer (publisher)|Springer]]
 |isbn=978-3-540-08356-6
 |mr=454485
}}<br/><br/> In this paper, Orno solves an eight-year-old problem posed by [[Ivan Singer]], according to ''Mathematical Reviews'' ({{MR|454485}}).<br/><br/>
* {{cite arXiv |last=Ørno |first=P. |year=1991 |title=On J. Borwein's concept of sequentially reflexive Banach spaces |eprint=math/9201233 }}<br/><br/> Here, Orno solved a problem posed by [[Jonathan M. Borwein]]. Orno characterized [[convergent sequence|sequentially]] [[reflexive space|reflexive]] [[Banach space]]s in terms of their lacking bad subspaces: Orno's theorem states that a Banach space ''X'' is sequentially reflexive if and only if the [[sequence space#.E2.84.93p spaces|space]] of [[absolute summability|absolutely summable sequence]]s [[sequence space#.E2.84.93p spaces|ℓ1]] is not isomorphic to a subspace of ''X''.

===Problem-solving===
Between 1976 and 1982, Peter Orno contributed problems or solutions that appeared in eighteen issues of ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'', which is published by the Mathematical Association of America (MAA).<ref>"Problems" sections of ''Mathematics Magazine'' in which Peter Orno is one of the contributing authors are: [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690199 Vol. 49, No. 3 (May 1976), pp. 149–154]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690127 Vol. 49, No. 4 (September 1976), pp. 211–218]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689756 Vol. 50, No. 1 (January 1977), pp. 46–53]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690222  Vol. 50, No. 4 (September 1977), pp. 211–216]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690154 Vol. 51, No. 2 (March 1978), pp. 127–132]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690005  Vol. 51, No. 3 (May 1978), pp. 193–201]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689475 Vol. 51, No. 4 (September 1978), pp. 245–249]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689977 Vol. 52, No. 1 (January 1979), pp. 46–55]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689851 Vol. 52, No. 2 (March 1979), pp. 113–118]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690284 Vol. 52, No. 3 (May 1979), pp. 179–184]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690032 Vol. 53, No. 1 (January 1980), pp. 49–54]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689961 Vol. 53, No. 2 (March 1980), pp. 112–117]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690110 Vol. 53, No. 3 (May 1980), pp. 180–186]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689622 Vol. 53, No. 4 (September 1980), pp. 244–251]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690443 Vol. 54, No. 2 (March 1981), pp. 84–87];  [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689635 Vol. 54, No. 4 (September 1981), pp. 211–214]; [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2689990 Vol. 54, No. 5 (November 1981), pp. 270–274]; and [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2690087 Vol. 55, No. 3 (May 1982), pp. 177–183].</ref> 
In 2006, Orno solved a problem in the ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'', another peer-reviewed journal of the MAA:

==Context==
Peter Orno is one of several pseudonymous contributors in the field of mathematics. Other pseudonymous mathematicians active in the 20th century include [[Nicolas Bourbaki]], [[John Rainwater]], [[John R. Isbell#Stanley|M.&nbsp;G.&nbsp;Stanley]], and [[John R. Isbell#Stanley|H.&nbsp;C.&nbsp;Enos]].<ref name="Phelps">Another pseudonymous mathematician, [[John Rainwater]], "is not as old or famous as N.&nbsp;Bourbaki (who may still be alive) but he is clearly older than Peter&nbsp;Orno .... (At least one of his authors had an interest in pornography, hence P. Orno.) He is also older than M.&nbsp;G.&nbsp;Stanley (with four papers) and H.&nbsp;C.&nbsp;Enoses [sic.] (with only two)." {{harv|Phelps|2002}}</ref>

==See also==
Besides connoting "pornography", the name "Ørno" features a non-standard symbol:
* [[Empty set|∅]], which symbolizes the [[empty set]] in mathematics.
* [[Œ|Ø]], an (archaic) English vowel, also denoted "OE", "Ö", and "Œ".
